name: A double prime (a″／エーダブルプライム)
reasoning: I tried to confirm the record's central claim that 'no wheat flour is used or baked anywhere on the premises' and could not source it anywhere. The quote 「こちらで売られている商品すべてがグルテンフリー」 is a food blogger's sentence on nagoya-meshi.com, not the shop's own words; the shop's own ABOUT page (adoubleprime.theshop.jp/about) says only 「グルテンフリーの焼き菓子店」 and 「管理栄養士の作る米粉のお菓子」, with no dedicated-facility claim, no allergen statement and no contamination information. Decisively, it is absent from all three curated gluten-free lists that DO include its Aichi peers — jp.japan-glutenfree.com's ~90-shop national list of bakeries where everything sold is GF, nagonavi's 2026 Nagoya GF top-5, and komeko-palette's Nagoya rice-bread guide — and I found no FindMeGlutenFree or HappyCow celiac review. With zero independent celiac-grade corroboration the dedicated bar fails outright, and since the surviving sources describe the product line rather than any GF handling, the two-independent-source bar for 'high' fails too.

name: Gluten Free BITTE (グルテンフリーBITTE)
reasoning: The shop's own claim is strong and specific (bitte2023.com: 「小麦不使用・完全グルテンフリーのお店です」 with 「コンタミネーションを徹底管理した」), so I attacked the corroboration instead — and both cited independent sources collapse. note.com/ladymo is a portfolio case study by 古田たかこ, the web designer BITTE hired to build its site, reservation system and LINE account, i.e. a paid vendor writing about her own client, and she explicitly does not describe the kitchen or any contamination protocol; komeko-palette.com is a self-promotional listicle published by こめこの店Palette, a rice-flour business that features itself in its own list. BITTE also does not appear on jp.japan-glutenfree.com's national fully-GF bakery list, on nagonavi's 2026 Nagoya list, or in any FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow celiac review I could find. That leaves the shop's unverified self-claim as the only source, which the HARD RULE caps at options/ask; the home-based operation now running just 「月1回の完全予約制」 (one day a month, reservation only, since April 2026) makes independent verification unlikely and access impractical.

komeko-palette source is a self-promotional listicle by a rice-flour business featured in its own list

identity_note: Business identity confirmed (グルテンフリー専門店 BITTE, 尾張旭市, Aichi; site live). name: Kashiya Fujinomiya (菓子屋 藤ノ宮)
reasoning: I tried to find a surviving wheat line, OEM wheat work, a 小麦 allergen declaration, or a contamination complaint, and found none. The company's own 会社概要 page carries the claim verbatim — 「2022年夏の動物ヨーチ製造終了に伴い、弊社では完全に小麦を使わないグルテンフリー食品製造を行うことにいたしました」 — and the discontinuation of 動物ヨーチ, its one wheat product, is independently documented on the Fujita Seika blog; the flagship 栗せん is a 白あん/rice senbei that never contained wheat, and the cakes are built from that same dough. Independent celiac-grade corroboration holds: jp.japan-glutenfree.com (the successor to the cited empacede URL) lists it ★★★★★ on its national roster of bakeries where everything sold is gluten-free, with the note 'no wheat flour used', and the oinagoya food blog plus Nagoya City's furusato-nozei listing both describe it as gluten-free. The genuine weakness is that the wheat wind-down was economic (小麦の高騰 plus inability to renew 駄菓子 equipment) rather than an allergen-safety decision, and no allergen testing, certification or cleaning protocol is published — but the facility has now run wheat-free for four years and nothing disconfirming surfaced.
red_flags: Factory made a wheat biscuit (動物ヨーチ) on shared confectionery equipment for decades until summer 2022; equipment was not replaced
Wheat was dropped for economic reasons (wheat price rises, cost of renewing 駄菓子 equipment), not as an allergen-safety policy
No published allergen testing, ppm threshold, certification or equipment-cleaning protocol
The record attributes a shared-equipment caveat to the empacede guide; that guide does not actually say this — the caveat is sound but the citation is wrong
All empacede URLs on the record are dead: glutenfree.empacede.co.jp now 301-redirects to jp.japan-glutenfree.com — sources need updating
oinagoya blog explicitly notes it does not verify facility-wide practices, only that individual products use rice flour
plain_rice: No — confectionery and bakery, no plain gohan served.

name: Kagome (香米豆ーkagomeー)
reasoning: Three separate attempts to disprove this one landed. First, the shop's own site claims only that its PRODUCTS use no wheat, dairy or egg (「当店の商品はすべて小麦・乳製品・卵不使用です」) — it never states the premises is wheat-free and never describes itself as a dedicated facility, so the own-claim half of the dedicated bar is not met at premises level. Second, the record cites the goguynet local-news article as corroborating evidence, but that article never mentions 小麦, gluten-free or allergens at all — it is a product review of the bread's texture, so the citation does not support what it is cited for. Third, the lineup includes 「オートミールを使ったちぎりパン」; uncertified oats in Japan are routinely cross-contaminated with wheat and barley during milling, which is a real celiac exposure route, and the record misframes this as an 'oat sensitivity' caution rather than a gluten-contamination one. That leaves jp.japan-glutenfree.com as the single genuine independent source, which the HARD RULE caps at options/ask.
red_flags: Uses oats (オートミールを使ったちぎりパン); oats in Japan are not certified GF and are commonly wheat/barley cross-contaminated at milling — a genuine celiac risk the record downplays as 'oat sensitivity'
Shop's own site makes a product-level claim only, never a premises-level wheat-free or dedicated-facility claim
Cited goguynet news article does not mention wheat, gluten-free or allergens anywhere — citation does not support the claim it is attached to
No cross-contamination statement published; the only caveat on the site concerns 白砂糖 in sourced ingredients
Only one genuine independent source (jp.japan-glutenfree.com); the cited empacede URL is dead and 301-redirects
Japan CAA warns 米粉 products frequently contain added wheat gluten or are made in wheat-handling rooms, with no mandatory contamination labelling
Open only 2nd and 4th weekends (Fri–Sun, 07:30–13:30) and sells out shortly after opening
plain_rice: No — bakery, no plain gohan served.
identity_note: The business is real and correctly described, but it is in 豊橋市杉山町 (Toyohashi), roughly 65 km and over an hour by train from Nagoya. The record files it under city 'nagoya' and calls Toyohashi 'Nagoya area', which is materially misleading for a city dining app. Reassign the city or scope it as an out-of-city day trip.

name: Bakeshop SolSol (グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店 Bakeshop SolSol)
reasoning: I went looking for a wheat line, a shared kitchen (the owner comes from a family of bread artisans, so a co-located wheat bakery was a live hypothesis), and any contamination complaint — and found none. The shop's own claim holds on its 商品へのこだわり page (「小麦グルテンを含む原材料は使用いたしません」, trading as a グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店), and independent celiac-grade corroboration is present: jp.japan-glutenfree.com lists it ★★★★★ on its national roster of bakeries where everything sold is gluten-free, noting 'all products contain no wheat'. Two further independent sources reinforce real GF handling: Chunichi Shimbun documents that owner 片山幸寛 built the business over 15 years to feed a nephew with a wheat allergy and that his 花酵母のカンパーニュ took the grand prize plus the グルテンフリー賞 at the 2nd 米粉パンコンテスト, and kodawarin.jp describes it as 「小麦を一切使わずに米粉パンを作るグルテンフリーパン専門店」 using 米粉100%. The one thing I could NOT verify is the record's headline quote about a separated kitchen — see red flags — but the dedicated bar is met without it.
